subject.title: fix(install): validate downloaded scripts before execution

question: Should OpenClaw permanently require every remotely downloaded Homebrew and NodeSource setup script to begin with `#!`, failing installation if an upstream serves otherwise-valid Bash in another format?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and improves rejection of error bodies, but the byte-level shebang requirement creates a new fail-closed compatibility contract with third-party installer endpoints that code review and CI cannot authorize on behalf of installer/security owners.

options.title: Approve the strict shebang gate
options.body: Land the current validator and accept that any non-shebang upstream response stops installation until OpenClaw or the upstream adjusts.

options.title: Use semantic Bash validation
options.body: Keep the explicit download guards and nonempty check, but replace the byte-level requirement with an owner-approved Bash syntax/content validation rule that permits valid shebang-less scripts.

options.title: Limit hardening to download failures
options.body: Merge only mandatory download-status checks and defer content validation, preserving maximum upstream compatibility but leaving HTTP-200 error bodies unguarded.

recommendation.title: Approve the strict shebang gate
recommendation.body: Land the current validator and accept that any non-shebang upstream response stops installation until OpenClaw or the upstream adjusts.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository identifies this handle as the overall product owner, and this choice changes the supported installer trust and failure boundary.
